problem_statement: said7388/developer-portfolio is a runnable Next.js 16 App Router developer portfolio (Tailwind CSS v4, SCSS, react-toastify) for the persona Abu Said, a full-stack developer. The single-page home composes a transparent identity nav, an animated hero, About, Experience, an auto-scrolling Skills marquee, a PROJECTS section of code-editor-style project cards, a Selected Case Studies section, Education, a Blog preview, and a Contact form, plus a separate /blog route that lists every post. Design and ship a real 'filter case studies by discipline' control on the Selected Case Studies section: a row of discipline tabs (All / Backend / Full-stack / AI) derived from the case studies' own discipline metadata that, when clicked, actually re-renders the case-study cards to the matching discipline and updates a genuine result count (for example 'Showing 2 of 6 case studies · Backend'). The case-study browser is shared and stays continuous across the portfolio: its title and index appear on the home page AND on the /blog route, while the full filterable card grid renders on the home page where the case studies live. Keep Abu Said's existing identity: the deep navy (#0d1224) surface, the teal (#16f2b3) and violet accents, the card-tile language, the illustration assets, and the responsive behaviour — the filter must read as part of the same site, keep its tab row and card grid within the 390px mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow, lay the cards out cleanly (no overlap or clipping), and emit no runtime console or network errors.
required_content: A real 'filter case studies by discipline' control (tabs All / Backend / Full-stack / AI) sits on the Selected Case Studies section; clicking a discipline tab re-renders the case-study cards to the matching discipline.
The control shows a genuine result count that re-derives from the active filter (e.g. 'Showing all 6 case studies' becomes 'Showing 2 of 6 case studies · Backend' when the Backend tab is selected).

The case-study browser (its title and index) is shared across the portfolio and appears on the home page AND on the /blog route (cross-page continuity); the full filterable card grid renders on the home page.

The filter tab row and the filtered card grid stay within the 390px mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow and lay out cleanly (cards wrap into a single column rather than spilling, overlapping, or clipping).

The filter adopts the portfolio's own deep-navy surface and teal (#16f2b3) accent, and the active tab is clearly legible (highlighted, not dark-on-dark) — an on-brand case-study browser, not an off-palette or broken control.

Each case study reuses an existing project illustration asset (crefin.jpg, travel.jpg, real-estate.jpg) and carries a title, an impact statement, technology tags, and a clear 'See related project' affordance; the PROJECTS, Skills, and Contact sections still render alongside the new filter, and all captured states emit no runtime console or network errors.
design_constraints: Preserve the portfolio's visual language: the deep-navy (#0d1224) surface, the teal (#16f2b3) impact text and violet section headers, the code-editor project cards, the auto-scrolling Skills marquee, and the section dividers; the filter and its cards must adopt this same dark-surface + teal identity.

Build the discipline tabs from the case studies' own discipline metadata, and render the shared case-study browser so a single component surfaces the index on both the home page and the /blog route rather than duplicating markup.

The filter tab row must wrap or shrink and stay within the mobile viewport at 390px, and the filtered card grid must reflow into a single column on narrow screens — do not pin the cards to a fixed desktop width or force them into a fixed-width non-wrapping row that overflows a phone or overlaps.

The result count and the visible card set must both re-derive from the live filter every render so they always match the selected tab; do not snapshot the grid or the count once and leave it stale when a tab is clicked.
Do not convert the site into a marketing landing page, blog index, or dashboard; it stays a single-persona developer portfolio with its home sections and the /blog route.
Reuse the template's own local illustration assets (public/image/crefin.jpg, travel.jpg, real-estate.jpg); do not introduce external stock imagery, remote fonts, or live third-party API calls.
state_constraints: desktop_initial captures the home hero and nav; the Selected Case Studies filter browser is present further down the page.
mobile_initial captures the home at 390px, where the case-study filter's tab row and card grid must stay within the viewport with no horizontal overflow.
desktop_projects scrolls to the PROJECTS section and confirms the existing project cards still render (regression).
desktop_case_studies scrolls to the Selected Case Studies section and captures the discipline-tab row, the result count, and the six case-study cards (All filter) laid out cleanly.
tablet_case_studies captures the Selected Case Studies section at tablet width; the tab row and grid stay readable within the viewport.
mobile_case_studies scrolls to the Selected Case Studies section at 390px and captures the tab row and card grid reflowed into a single column within the viewport.

desktop_filter_backend captures the Selected Case Studies section after clicking the 'Backend' discipline tab: the grid re-filters to the two backend case studies and the count updates to 'Showing 2 of 6 case studies · Backend'.
mobile_filter_backend captures the same Backend-filtered view at 390px, reflowed cleanly within the viewport.
desktop_skills scrolls to the Skills marquee and confirms it still renders (regression).
desktop_blog captures the /blog route; the shared case-study browser (its title and index) must also be present here (cross-page continuity).

change_completion: The Selected Case Studies section has a working discipline-filter control (All / Backend / Full-stack / AI) on home.
Clicking a discipline tab re-renders the case-study cards to that discipline and updates the result count to reflect it.
The Abu Said persona (hero, PROJECTS cards, Skills marquee, Contact) remains intact alongside the filter.
The home page and the /blog route stay reachable through the existing nav.
design_consistency: The filter and cards adopt the portfolio's deep-navy surface and teal (#16f2b3) accent, with a legible highlighted active tab.
The shared case-study browser rides both the home page and the /blog route (title + index).
The card-tile visual language and typography are preserved across the filter and the existing sections.
regression: The PROJECTS section and its code-editor project cards still render on home.
The case-study browser appears on the /blog route, not only on home, confirming cross-page continuity.
The Skills marquee and the Contact section still render their content.
responsive: 390px home has no horizontal overflow; the filter tab row wraps/shrinks and stays within the viewport.
The filtered card grid reflows into a single column on mobile without spilling, overlapping, or clipping.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Next.js 16 App Router portfolio task at L4 on said7388/developer-portfolio, capability=Consistency, scope=section. The graded change designs the portfolio's OWN Selected Case Studies filter: a discipline-tab control (All / Backend / Full-stack / AI) built from the case studies' discipline metadata that actually re-renders the cards and updates a real result count, with the case-study index shared across the home page and the /blog route. Four orthogonal machine-checked gates: no_horizontal_overflow on the 390px mobile home and mobile case-studies (the filter grid must reflow into one column, not pin cards to a fixed desktop width); visual_regression on the case-study filter crops at desktop/mobile case-studies + the Backend-filtered view (on-brand deep-navy #0d1224 surface + teal #16f2b3 accent with a legible active tab and a clean card grid, not an overlapping shingled grid with an illegible tab); cross-page dom_assertions that the case-study browser (cs-filter__title 'Selected case studies') rides the /blog route as well as home; and interaction_assertions that clicking the Backend tab re-filters the grid and updates the count to 'Showing 2 of 6 case studies' (a snapshotted grid+count that never re-derives fails this). The baseline is the original layout defect (case-study grid pinned to a fixed 460px-per-card non-wrapping track, present on home only) which fails overflow + visual + cross-page but passes interaction; the known-bad 'smart wrong' filter keeps a denser off-layout grid with negative gutters so the six cards overlap and clip, is home-only, and snapshots its grid and count at mount so the tab click succeeds but the terminal result stays stale, failing all four gates. INFRA fixes applied identically to all three legs (not part of the graded change): next/font/google Inter replaced with a local font stack; the runtime dev.to articles fetch on the home page and /blog route replaced with an in-repo blog fixture; and Next image optimization disabled so the local /image illustration assets serve fully offline. The local illustration assets crefin.jpg, travel.jpg, real-estate.jpg are reused as-is for the case-study cards.
